extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and screenwriters (esp. episodic TV; also novelists and short-fiction authors)
extracted.subtask_description: A practical guide to structuring a character-driven story using Dan Harmon's eight-step Story Circle (a simplified Hero's Journey) to plot episodic TV, novels, or short fiction and to ensure a clear character arc and transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: You (Comfort Zone)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish protagonist in their normal world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set a clear baseline: who the protagonist is and what their ordinary life looks like. This establishes what will be disrupted and provides the initial emotional/psychological state that must change. (Paired with 'Find' as a mirrored counterpoint.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Need
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a concrete desire, absence, or lack that drives the protagonist into action. This motivates the crossing of the threshold and anchors the story's goal. (Paired with 'Take'.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Go
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross the threshold into the unfamiliar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the protagonist leaving their comfort zone—physically, emotionally, or circumstantially—so the stakes of the journey are clear. The crossing must feel real and consequential (see 'Threshold crossing is real'). (Paired with 'Return'.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Search (Adapt/Struggle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt to the new world; encounter obstacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict the protagonist's attempts to navigate the unfamiliar environment, including struggles, learning, and adaptation. This phase should create momentum and complicate the pursuit of the 'Need'. (Paired with 'Change'.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Find
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have the protagonist obtain or achieve the sought-after object/goal/insight—either actually or superficially. This step mirrors 'You' and should reveal how the attainment contrasts with the original ordinary state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take (Pay the Price)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost; loss; sacrifice; reality check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a meaningful cost, loss, or sacrifice that accompanies or follows attainment—this is essential to make the transformation feel earned. Without a real price, the change can feel unearned or hollow. (Mirrors 'Need'.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Return
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the protagonist coming back toward the ordinary world (or to a new normal) after the events in the unfamiliar realm. The return should contrast with the initial 'You' state and set up the final integration of change. (Mirrors 'Go'.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Change
rubrics_metrics.description: They are transformed; the familiar world reads differently now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate the protagonist's internal transformation and how their perspective or circumstances have altered the original ordinary world. The transformation must be visible and consequential—this is the payoff of the arc. (Mirrors 'Search'.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the story so each early step has a meaningful counterpart later on; use these mirrored relationships to highlight change and thematic resonance. The circle's balance helps clarify how events oppose/answer each other across the arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: the final state must be different from initial state
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the protagonist's end-state is meaningfully distinct from their beginning; the arc should show cause-and-effect progression (actions, sacrifices, learning) that justify the change rather than asserting change without groundwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: The cost matters / Threshold must be real
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost matters — without sacrifice/loss in step 6, the change feels unearned; Threshold crossing is real — the protagonist must genuinely leave their comfort zone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two interrelated checkpoints: (1) Make the protagonist pay a real price (emotional, relational, material) so the arc has weight; (2) Make the 'Go' step a genuine departure from the status quo so subsequent adaptation and growth are credible. Both prevent hollow or token transformations.
